newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ELPO JEANS MAKER TO ENTER BOURSE FEB/JAN.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ELPO JEANS MAKER TO ENTER BOURSE FEB/JAN.

text.p: Polish garment maker Elpo SA, whose initial public offering ends on Friday, has pushed up its planned bourse entry to late January or early February from March, a company board member said on Wednesday.
"We expect it (the bourse entry) in late Janurary or early February so investors won't have to wait so long," Teresa Pituch told Reuters.
She said the public offering's 600,000 shares at 22 zlotys each would likely be taken up without the help of the underwriter, Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA.
Elpo, whose full name is Zaklady Przemyslu Odziezowego Elpo SA and specialises in denim clothes, plans to enter the bourse's parallel market.
It expects net profits to grow to 1.3 million zlotys in 1996, 1.8 million in 1997, 2.5 million in 1998 and 3.4 million in 2000 from last year's 0.4 million zlotys.
It sees sales rising to 13.8 million zlotys in 1996, 16.9 million in 1997, 23.1 million in 1998 and 31.3 million zlotys in 2000 from last year's 12.9 million zlotys.
